# Regression test for two real incidents: an unrecognized `--flag`-shaped token
# (most commonly a bare --help/-h) used to silently land in a required
# positional slot instead of being rejected -- `breeze register identity --help`
# registered a real identity literally named "--help" (leaking its token to
# stdout), and `breeze acquire lock --help` silently acquired a real exclusive
# lock on the literal path "--help". Neither must ever happen again, for any
# subcommand, not just the ones originally reported.
env BREEZE_DIR=$WORK/state

# Bare top-level --help/-h exits cleanly (0), same as any subcommand's. usage()
# prints to stderr (it doubles as the no-args/unknown-command error path).
exec breeze --help
stderr 'usage: breeze <verb> <noun>'
exec breeze -h
stderr 'usage: breeze <verb> <noun>'

# --help exits cleanly (0) and just prints usage — no mutation.
exec breeze register identity --help
stdout 'usage: breeze register identity'
exec breeze ps --json
stdout '\{\}'

exec breeze acquire lock --help
stdout 'usage: breeze acquire lock'
exec breeze list locks --json
stdout '"locks":\s*\[\]'

# A genuine typo'd flag must error clearly too, not silently register/acquire
# using the flag text as the intended value.
! exec breeze register identity alice --tokne foo
stderr 'unrecognized flag "--tokne"'
exec breeze ps --json
stdout '\{\}'

exec breeze stop
